newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Most of Portugal's elite want EMU referendum - poll.
newsitem.headline: Most of Portugal's elite want EMU referendum - poll.

text.p: Most of Portugal's top politicians, civil servants and business people favour a referendum on the Maastricht Treaty, according to a poll by a Lisbon college published in a newspaper on Thursday.

The poll by the Superior Institute of Corporate and Labour Studies, made available to Diario de Noticias newspaper, said 76 percent of MPs, ministers, local government and party leaders, senior civil servants and business people backed a referendum.
It said 21 percent opposed such a vote.
Diario de Noticias did not give the size of the sample interviewed or say when the poll was conducted.
The poll said 77 percent favoured Portugal's participation in the planned European single currency, or euro. Fourteen percent wanted to stay outside Economic and Monetary Union.

The ruling Socialist Party (PS) and main opposition Social Democratic Party (PSD), which both favour Portugal's participation in the euro, have said that only revisions to the Maastricht Treaty should be subject to a referendum.
The small right-wing Popular Party, which has just 15 seats in the 230-seat parliament, has called for a referendum.
The PS and PSD staged a rare show of unity on Wednesday, agreeing a joint motion to parliament backing the country's bid to join EMU in the first wave in 1999.

The motion will be put to parliament, where the two parties hold a combined 85 percent of the seats, in a debate on Thursday in which Prime Minister Antonio Guterres and Finance Minister Antonio Sousa Franco will take part.
